20-Minute Writing Lesson · A2

The Grammar
of a Letter

Read a letter. Find its word pictures. Put the words in the right order. Write your own.

ReadAnswerFindOrderPracticeWrite
Part 1 · Read the letter

Read it aloud.

The letter is the news. One voice — the whole pair. Skip nothing — don't stop for the grammar, just enjoy the story.

Dear Jack, ✉

Hi! How are you? Sorry I've taken so long to answer, but my computer broke down last week and I only managed to get it working today. Anyway, I'm really glad your sister is visiting London.

The best place for her to go shopping is Camden Town in north-west London. There is a huge variety of colourful indoor and outdoor flea markets, international food stalls, clothes stalls, music stalls and street vendors. There's nothing you can't find at Camden Market, from vintage clothing to antiques, all at bargain prices! I was there last Saturday with my friend Jili. She bought a beautiful embroidered handbag that goes with all her clothes and I bought a pair of 70s style second-hand jeans, some rare comic books for my collection, and a small leather purse, all for £15. Can you believe it? After our shopping, Jili and I enjoyed some Chinese rice noodles and sweet and sour chicken at one of the food stalls.

I'm sure your sister will find what she wants there. London is a great place for shopping, and I'd be glad to show her round if she wants.

Have to go now. I've got a project to finish for Monday.

Your friend,
Evelyn

Camden Market — her sister's weekend

Answer the four questions — in your own words

Part 2 · Answer

Answer the questions — in your own words.

1.Who is writing this letter? Who is it for?
2.What is Evelyn's sister going to do?
3.Where does she go shopping?
4.What has Jili bought? What has Evelyn bought?

Answer aloud — the whole pair can hear the same voice

Part 3 · Find

Find the word pictures in big letters.

Four clusters from the letter. Say each one out loud, then find it in the letter again.

Cluster 1beautiful embroidered handbagopinion + participle
Cluster 2second-hand jeansage — a compound
Cluster 3small leather pursesize → material
Cluster 4Chinese rice noodlesorigin
Part 4 · Order

Where does beautiful sit?

Read the sentence through the four dolls. Point at each one. What do you notice?

Opinion→Age→Origin→Material→Noun
The poster sentence — say it in order A beautiful old Russian wooden nesting doll.

Say the order. Point at the dolls. Then — where does beautiful go?

Opinion · Age · Origin · Material · Noun

Part 5 · Practice

Fix the order. In your notebook.

Five sentences. Every opinion first, noun closest to the end. Write the fixed sentence down.

1.Ann bought a square / small / wooden table.
2.Steve wore a navy blue / woollen / second-hand pair of gloves.
3.Sarah gave them a beautiful / round / silver frame.
4.Her grandmother has a gold / old / Russian pair of earrings.
5.He bought her a striped / cotton / modern bag.

Write the fixed sentence — then check on the next page

Part 6 · Write

Write your reply.

Your own news — the same letter. One required cluster in the body — the words are jumbled. Put them in the right order. That is the whole point.

GreetingHi ___, ReasonI'm writing because… ___ Body — the required cluster — jumbled… I bought a wooden / nesting / Russian / beautiful / old / doll ClosingWrite back soon! ___

Write it now — put the adjectives in the right order — 100–120 words. Then read it aloud.

Your letter — the same structure
Part 7 · Check

Two boxes. One correction per line.

✓

Your letter

Greeting · reason for writing · body · closing · your name — as Evelyn signs it.

✓

Your cluster

Show me your beautiful. Where does it sit? Opinion always comes first — the outermost shell.

Practice — the five answers
  • 1. a small square wooden table
  • 2. a second-hand navy blue woollen pair of gloves
  • 3. a beautiful round silver frame
  • 4. a(n) old Russian gold pair of earrings
  • 5. a modern striped cotton bag

Check the practice. Fix the one thing — one correction per line.

Exit the lesson

A beautiful old Russian wooden nesting doll.

Read your letter aloud. Then say it together — opinion always comes first — the outermost shell. The letter is your own.

Say the sentence out loud — together. Then read your letter aloud.
